messages:
Lee Rodriguez: Quick UX review: timeseries y-axis unit toggle. Current mock has a three-button group (Auto / Raw / Normalize) but it's taking a lot of space. Proposal: one compact chevron toggle that cycles states and shows current unit + accessible label. Also consider a tiny sparkline preview inside the control to indicate effect. Thoughts?

Maria Chen: I like the compactness but worried about discoverability. Maybe show the full label on hover and keep an affordance "Units: Auto" as text collapsed on narrow screens. Sparkline preview is neat for power users.

Samir Patel: Microcopy: keep it simple. Tooltip on hover: "Units: Auto (click to cycle: Auto → Raw → Normalized)". When focused with keyboard read: "YAxis units: Auto. Press Enter to cycle units."

Jon Park: Implementation note: if Normalize recomputes per-series baselines it can be expensive on large dashboards. We should debounce changes and run normalization in a web worker or backend aggregate. Also caching normalized series per-query window.

Lee Rodriguez: Great call on performance. We'll show a loading spinner inside the control during recompute instead of freezing charts. Debounce 250ms and use worker off-main-thread.

Tia Nguyen: Accessibility: ensure the control has clear ARIA states and keyboard cycle order. Suggest role=button with aria-pressed or aria-expanded? Example:

```
<button class=\"unit-toggle\" role=\"button\" aria-label=\"YAxis units: Auto. Press Enter to change to Raw\">Units: Auto</button>
```

Also: provide a preference to keep units persistent per dashboard.

Samir Patel: UX nit: when Normalized is on, show a soft label on the Y axis like "(normalized)" and add a short hover hint "Normalized: each series scaled to its max". Avoid long copy.

Maria Chen: Outlier handling related to this: propose "Outlier pinning" option in the axis menu. Instead of stretching the scale, pinned outliers render as capped markers above the chart with a "+N" badge. Keeps visual context but preserves readability.

Jon Park: Agree, overflow badge is straightforward. We should also expose the threshold value in the legend (e.g., ">= 1000") and allow users to click the badge to expand a list of pinned points.

Lee Rodriguez: Smoothing discussion: rather than a binary smoothing toggle, propose adaptive smoothing that changes kernel strength by zoom level. At full zoom smoothing=0 (raw), at overview smoothing=high. Also keep manual toggle override.

Tia Nguyen: Be careful: smoothing can hide accessibility-critical spikes (e.g., error events). Make sure the help copy explains tradeoffs and add a "Show raw markers" overlay option so spikes are still detectable by screenreader and visually.

Samir Patel: Suggested copy for help icon: "Smoothing reduces noise for trend view. Raw markers show individual points." Tooltip: "Smoothing: automatic by zoom. Toggle to override."

Lee Rodriguez: UX flows: 1) Compact unit toggle with sparkline + hover label. 2) Outlier pinning with overflow badge and click-to-expand detail. 3) Adaptive smoothing + manual override + "Show raw markers" overlay. 4) Persist user choice per dashboard.

Designbot: Updated figma frame: https://www.figma.com/file/wxyz7890/timeseries-axis-controls — frame: "axis/compact-units-overflow-v2" :sparkles:

Maria Chen: Nice. Action items: I'll update mocks with the sparkline inside control and overflow badge. Samir, can you draft the inline copy? Tia, can you add a11y checks for keyboard cycle and screenreader readouts? Jon, please confirm perf approach (worker + cache).

Jon Park: On it 1: will prototype worker flow and report perf numbers.

Samir Patel: Drafting copy now, will post PR to figma comments.

Tia Nguyen: I'll run keyboard + screenreader tests and add to the a11y checklist.

Lee Rodriguez: Thanks all 60; we'll aim to move to a design-implement ticket after updated mocks.
